zh.sourceText: 吃素比吃肉更健康。数据显示，素食者的心血管疾病发生率明显低于肉食者，平均寿命也更长。既然素食能降低疾病风险、延长寿命，我们每个人都不妨试试以植物为主的饮食。不过，这个结论悄悄藏了一个假设：素食者更低的发病率完全来自饮食本身，而不是因为他们整体上更注重健康、更常运动、更少抽烟。某植物奶品牌在超市门口试饮：『植物力量，喝出健康！』

textRefs.conclusion_1: 我们每个人都不妨试试以植物为主的饮食
textRefs.reason_1: 素食者的心血管疾病发生率明显低于肉食者，平均寿命也更长
textRefs.assumption_1: 素食者更低的发病率完全来自饮食本身，而不是因为他们整体上更注重健康、更常运动、更少抽烟

hints: 先找结论和支撑它的数据理由
去挖掘区：发病率低一定归因于吃素吗？
健康的生活方式可能同时解释了『吃素』和『少生病』
zh.explanation: 结论是「不妨试试以植物为主的饮食」，理由是『素食者心血管疾病率更低』。但这个论证默认：更低发病率完全由饮食造成。可另一种可能同样成立——选择吃素的人往往也更注重锻炼、更少抽烟，是这些因素（而非素食本身）带来了健康。这就是「相关性不等于因果」的经典陷阱：找假设时，永远要问『还有别的解释吗？』

en.sourceText: Eating vegetarian is healthier than eating meat. Data shows that vegetarians have significantly lower rates of cardiovascular disease than meat-eaters, and they also live longer on average. Since a plant-based diet lowers disease risk and extends life, we should all try eating mostly plants. This conclusion, however, quietly assumes that vegetarians' lower disease rates come entirely from their diet — not from the fact that they tend to be more health-conscious overall, exercising more and smoking less. A plant-milk brand is giving out samples at the supermarket entrance: 'Plant power, drink your way to health!'

textRefs.conclusion_1: we should all try eating mostly plants
textRefs.reason_1: vegetarians have significantly lower rates of cardiovascular disease than meat-eaters
textRefs.assumption_1: vegetarians' lower disease rates come entirely from their diet — not from the fact that they tend to be more health-conscious overall, exercising more and smoking less

hints: Find the conclusion and the statistical reason supporting it
Head to the dig site: is the lower disease rate really caused by the diet?
A healthy lifestyle could explain both 'being vegetarian' and 'fewer illnesses'
en.explanation: The conclusion is 'we should all try eating mostly plants', supported by 'vegetarians have lower cardiovascular rates'. But the argument assumes diet alone causes the lower rate. Another equally plausible story: people who choose vegetarianism also tend to exercise more and smoke less — those factors, not the diet itself, drive the health gains. This is the classic 'correlation is not causation' trap. When digging for assumptions, always ask: 'Is there another explanation?'
